subject: Geography
preamble: The Geography syllabus is designed to evaluate candidates' understanding of spatial patterns, physical processes, and human-environment interactions. It emphasizes map reading, practical techniques, field work methods, regional geography with special reference to Nigeria and Africa, and global geographical concepts.
aims: Handle and interpret topographical maps, photographs, statistical data, diagrams, and basic field survey results;
Demonstrate knowledge of man's physical and human environment and how man lives and earns a living on the Earth's surface with special reference to Nigeria and Africa;
Show understanding of the interrelationship between man and his environment;
Apply geographical concepts, skills, and principles to solving real-world problems;
Understand field work techniques and the practical study of a local area in the field.
requirements: Candidates should be equipped with standard drawing and survey instruments, including rulers, protractors, pairs of compasses, and graph papers for map work.
Calculators may be used where quantitative analysis, map scale conversions, or statistical calculations are required.

examination_scheme.summary: The examination tests candidates across practical, physical, human, and regional geography domains through objective, practical, and essay-based assessment formats.

papers.title: Objective Test
papers.details: Consists of multiple choice objective questions covering practical, physical, human, and regional geography topics.

papers.title: Essay and Practical Paper
papers.details: Consists of essay questions and practical map reading/interpretation tasks requiring detailed responses, cross-profiles, data interpretation, and regional case studies.

topics.title: 1. Maps and Scale Measurement
topics.notes: Types and uses of maps; scale types and conversions; measurement of distances, areas, reduction and enlargement; directions, bearings, and gradients on topographical maps.

topics.title: 2. Map Reading, Interpretation, and Statistical Representation
topics.notes: Drawing cross-profiles and determining intervisibility; recognition and description of physical and human features on topographical maps; computation and interpretation of statistical data, charts, and diagrams.

topics.title: 3. Elementary Surveying and Geographic Information Systems (GIS)
topics.notes: Surveying techniques: chain and prismatic compass, open and closed traverses, procedures, problems, advantages, and disadvantages; GIS components, techniques, data sources (remote sensing, digitizing, scanning), applications (defense, agriculture, rural development), and challenges in Nigeria.

topics.title: 4. Field Work and Local Field Study
topics.notes: Fieldwork techniques, methods of data collection, observation, field sketching, interviewing, equipment handling, data presentation, analysis, and reporting in local area geographical studies.

topics.title: 5. The Earth as a Planet and the Earth's Crust
topics.notes: Solar system position, rotation, revolution, shape, size; latitude (distance) and longitude (time); internal and external structure; four spheres and energy/water cycle relationships; rock types, characteristics, formation, and uses; tectonic forces.

topics.title: 6. Major Landforms, Volcanism, Earthquakes, and Denudation
topics.notes: Mountains, plateaux, plains, coastal, karst, and desert landforms; volcanic landforms, origin, types, and earthquake events; tropical denudation processes: weathering, erosion, mass movement, and deposition by water, wind, and waves.

topics.title: 7. Water Bodies, Weather, Climate, and Vegetation
topics.notes: Oceans, seas, and ocean currents (distribution, causes, effects, uses); lakes and river courses; weather and climate elements, factors, and measuring instruments; Greek and Köppen climate classifications; basic science of climate change; plant growth factors, plant succession, vegetation types, distribution, and human impact.

topics.title: 8. Soils, Environmental Resources, Ecosystems, and Hazards
topics.notes: Soil properties, formation factors, profiles, tropical soil types, and human impact; renewable vs. non-renewable environmental resources; land ecosystems, balance, and human impacts; natural and human-induced environmental hazards (drought, flooding, deforestation, pollution, desertification) and prevention/conservation methods.

topics.title: 9. Population Dynamics and Distribution
topics.notes: World population patterns (Amazon Basin, N.E. USA, India, Japan, West Coast of Southern Africa); birth/death rates, age/sex structure; distribution factors, growth problems, and migration types, causes, and effects.

topics.title: 10. Settlement Systems
topics.notes: Rural and urban settlement patterns (dispersed, nucleated, linear); factors influencing location, growth, and functions of settlements; urban problems and rural-urban interrelationships with reference to Western Europe, USA, Middle East, and West Africa.

topics.title: 11. Selected Economic Activities
topics.notes: Primary, secondary, tertiary, and quaternary activities; agricultural systems, factors, and problems; manufacturing industries, locational factors, distribution, and tropical African industrialization issues; transportation/communication modes and economic roles; world trade patterns and commodity routes; tourism importance, problems, and solutions.

topics.title: 12. Physical and Human Setting of Nigeria
topics.notes: Location, size, political states, boundaries, neighbours, and ethnic groups; geology, relief, landforms, climate, drainage, vegetation, and soils of Nigeria; population size, distribution, migration, and natural resource conservation.

topics.title: 13. Economic Geography of Nigeria
topics.notes: Agricultural systems and development challenges; manufacturing industries, product distribution, and locational factors; transportation and communication modes; regional and international trade dynamics; tourism importance and destination management.

topics.title: 14. Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS)
topics.notes: Meaning, historical development, objectives, and mandate of ECOWAS; member states identification; advantages, prospects, trade integration challenges, and proposed solutions.
